title: Hear me out: maybe Norway should give Melania Trump the Nobel peace prize | Arwa Mahdawi
text:
Haters be damned: Donald Trump just keeps on winning. He won the inaugural Fifa peace prize last year and was presented with the completely real, totally not made-up “Man of the Century” award at a recent rally. The president has also spent the greater part of a decade claiming he was once crowned Michigan’s Man of the Year: a fantastic achievement considering there is no such award and Trump has never lived in Michigan.
But despite his many trophies, there is one honour that has proved elusive: the Nobel peace prize. Trump holds a bit of a grudge about that, recently terming Norway a “shithouse country” for passing him over for the award. In response, the country’s tourism board highlighted some of its nicest public lavatories with the tagline: “Norway makes shit houses great again!”
Speaking in my capacity as Philadelphia’s Woman of the Millennium, I’ve got a modest proposal for the people of Norway. The toilet gag was excellent, but if they want to do some top-tier trolling then I think next year’s Nobel peace prize needs to go to Melania Trump.
Some people would be thrilled for their spouse to be in the spotlight, but I’m not sure that’s the case with Donald. Indeed, the president has said: “You can only have … one star in a family; it doesn’t work with two.” If Melania got Trump’s coveted Nobel peace prize, it could spark a war in the White House.
But look, I’m not just suggesting the Norwegians honour Melania because it would raise Donald’s blood pressure. No, it seems Melania has become quite the diplomat. Last week, the White House announced that the first lady had “successfully secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, localized to the city of Oleshky”.
How on earth did she manage that? Apparently, Melania initiated discussions with Russia and Ukraine and “aligned the parties on the agreement’s objectives, technical procedures, timing, processes, and terms, in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary”.
Whatever all that means, it seems to have worked: the ceasefire went into effect on Tuesday in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city, which has been enduring a worsening humanitarian crisis. On Friday, hundreds of people were evacuated from the frontline town and emergency supplies were brought in for people who needed to stay.
Melania has been widely praised for brokering this ceasefire. Melania’s adviser has claimed she “singlehandedly” secured it, adding that no other first lady has ever achieved what Melania just pulled off, and she is “completely revamping the role of first lady … [and] saving lives.”
Perhaps. But if there is one thing that the Trumps are good at it, it is taking credit for other people’s work. So is the first lady really the great peacemaker that she’s making herself out to be?
To be fair, Melania has done some good work vis-à-vis Ukraine and certainly seems to be better at peacemaking than Jared Kushner is, who has made huge sums of money while operating as one of Trump’s top diplomatic envoys to the Middle East. Last year, for example, Melania wrote a letter to Vladimir Putin pleading for Ukrainian children seized by Russia to be returned to their families. Since then, her office has said she’s facilitated numerous rounds of family reunification.
However, despite the claim that Melania “singlehandedly” secured this ceasefire, it would appear she had a little help. Pope Leo XIV also personally appealed to Putin about the situation in Oleshky in early October. It’s unclear whether he had more or less sway than the first lady had, but the pope is certainly being rather more modest about his involvement.
So what’s next for Melania after her success in Oleshky? In an interview with Newsmax, her adviser Marc Beckman said Melania might help pave the way to “durable, everlasting peace” in Ukraine and Russia as a whole.
“She’s against war, she thinks it’s senseless … she wants to see peace all over the world,” Beckman added.
Does she indeed? In that case she might want to have a word with the president, who started a very bloody war against Iran and who is currently trying to use US taxpayer money to send 2,000lb bombs to Israel, a country accused of genocide.
Forget the Nobel peace prize. If Melania can do something about her husband, I’m crowning her Michigan’s Woman of the Year.
Bad news for US women trying to manage menopause symptoms
Last November, the FDA announced that menopausal hormone therapy medications would no longer require a scary “black-box” label on them, which is the highest safety-related warning a medication can have. This reassured a lot of women about the treatment and caused a surge in demand. Supply didn’t keep up, and there’s been a shortage of estrogen patches in the US all year because of an uptick in demand. Now Reuters reports that the shortage has spread beyond estrogen patches “with some injectable and vaginal estrogen products also in short supply”.
Dolores Huerta, labor leader and civil rights champion, dies aged 96
Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers union (UFW), which improved conditions for agricultural workers in the 1960s and 1970s. She is also credited with coining the phrase “Sí, se puede!” (yes, we can), which was UFW’s slogan and then Barack Obama’s 2008 campaign rally cry.
Kamala Harris advises Democrats not to impeach Trump if they win House and Senate
“I think that going in the direction of impeachment is not a good idea,” Harris said in a MeidasTouch interview. “I was in the Senate for the last go-round, and the votes aren’t there.” In other words: don’t hold your breath that Trump will face immediate accountability if the Democrats dominate the midterms.
Egypt continues crackdown on press freedom and fines editor Lina Attalah
Attalah is the editor-in-chief of Madr Masar, an independent Egyptian news site that has frequently been critical of the Egyptian president Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi’s government. The government recently accused her of running a website without a license, detained her, and shut down Mada Masr. The crackdown “can only mean that Egypt’s security agencies are moving from years of harassing independent media to wiping them out completely”, one expert told the Guardian.
The toxic legacy of body positivity
“We are living through a strange time in the language around bodies,” writes Hannah Marriott in the Guardian. The body positivity era is over, but “much of its social training lingers.” Thanks to the GLP-1 boom, everyone is shrinking, but it’s taboo to talk about it. “What we’re left with is a world in which skinny bodies are lionized in fashion, culture and daily life, but to either admit a desire to conform, or express concern about it, feels socially verboten.”
Queer romance is dead: Chrishell Stause and G Flip have broken up
You may be familiar with this viral tweet: “I’m 50. All celebrity news looks like this: ‘Curtains for Zoosha? K-smog and Batboy caught flipping a grunt.’” I am still a mere 43, but I had my own curtains for Zoosha moment this week when I saw the headlines about G Flip, which I could have sworn was a watch. If you are similarly confused, Rebecca Shaw has an explainer as to why some of the queer community are in mourning.
- Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
